articles.title: Islam Has Three Names Left on His Hit List #ufc
articles.description: Islam Makhachev has revealed his own hit list — and Chael Sonnen thinks it's one of the coolest things a champion can say. According to Islam, there are three names left that he wants to handle before he's finished with the sport: Carlos Prates, Michael Morales, and Shavkat Rakhmonov. Chael agrees that those are the three guys. But completing that list won't happen quickly. Three fights could take roughly a year and a half, especially when injuries, scheduling, and the realities of MMA are factored in. And there are still plenty of unanswered questions. Can Islam beat Prates? Can he beat Morales? Can he beat Rakhmonov? We don't know — and that's exactly why the fights have to happen. Chael also discusses Rakhmonov's injury and why time away from competition doesn't make an athlete better. If you're not training and competing, you're not developing your skills. When Rakhmonov eventually returns, he'll have to prove he's still the same fighter. But the bigger story is Islam's mindset. He's essentially telling the world: I'm not leaving until I handle this business. Three elite contenders. Three massive challenges. And a champion who apparently wants to settle all of it himself. #IslamMakhachev #CarlosPrates #MichaelMorales #ShavkatRakhmonov #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #UFCNews #MMAAnalysis #UFCChampionship

articles.title: Name 15 UFC Heavyweights Better Than Gable
articles.description: Why isn't Gable Steveson ranked in the UFC heavyweight division? Chael Sonnen doesn't buy the explanation. The rankings committee says a fighter generally has to beat someone already inside the top 15 before earning a spot. But Chael points out that once fighters are ranked, the committee moves them up and down constantly even when they haven't competed. So why is breaking into the rankings treated differently? Chael challenges anyone to name 15 UFC heavyweights they genuinely believe would beat Gable Steveson. He also brings Jon Jones into the discussion: Dana White has repeatedly said that if Jones returns, he'll fight for a title, despite Jones currently being unranked. If an unranked fighter can immediately fight for a championship, what exactly are the rankings supposed to represent? Chael argues that rankings matter for matchmaking, contracts, sponsorships and fighter careers so if the UFC is going to publish them, the committee should rank who they actually believe are the best fighters. And Chael doesn't believe anyone truly thinks 15 UFC heavyweights are better than Gable Steveson. #GableSteveson #UFC #ChaelSonnen #JonJones #MMA Bad Guy Inc merch now available at https://BadGuyInc.com Click here to subscribe: https://bit.ly/3FrHIPK Follow me on IG: https://bit.ly/3HY7BIE Follow me on Twitter: https://bit.ly/3tvY5J7 Follow me on Threads https://www.threads.com/@sonnench

articles.title: Islam Makhachev Has Already Peaked #ufc
articles.description: Why are Islam Makhachev's fights getting harder? Chael Sonnen believes the answer isn't that his opponents are suddenly bigger, stronger, or better at 170 pounds. Islam's element of surprise is gone. His opponents are beginning to understand exactly what he's trying to do. They've studied him, prepared for his wrestling, and figured out how to make his signature style more difficult to execute. Islam has said that these fights are getting closer and that he needs to improve. Chael loves the mentality — but he doesn't believe the improvement Islam is talking about is actually possible. According to Chael, Islam has reached the point in his career where he's essentially topped out. He may be able to maintain his current level, but he's unlikely to become significantly better from here. And that's an entirely different challenge. When you've reached the highest level of the sport, the goal isn't necessarily to keep improving. It's to maintain what you've built while everyone else continues trying to catch you. That takes enormous mental discipline. Islam is still ahead of the field. But if his opponents now understand him better, can he maintain that advantage long enough to remain champion? #IslamMakhachev #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #UFCNews #MMAAnalysis #Islam #UFC170 #MMAChampionship #CombatSports

articles.title: Charles Oliveira Is NOT Getting the Next Title Shot
articles.description: Charles Oliveira believes he should be next for Justin Gaethje and Chael Sonnen admits his argument is incredibly difficult to dismiss. Oliveira is the reigning BMF champion, a former UFC lightweight champion and one of the biggest stars in the division. More importantly, he's already beaten Gaethje. He didn't just win a decision he stopped him without losing a round. So why doesn't Chael believe Charles will get the next undisputed title shot? It comes down to the fight with Arman Tsarukyan that never happened. Chael explains why UFC history makes it difficult to imagine Oliveira pulling out of that matchup and then immediately being rewarded with a championship opportunity, particularly with Arman and Mauricio Ruffy still trying to establish who belongs at the front of the line. But that doesn't leave Oliveira without a major fight. Chael believes Charles should embrace his position as BMF champion and there's one matchup he finds considerably more exciting than another fight with Gaethje: Paddy Pimblett vs. Charles Oliveira. articles.title: Stop Celebrating on the UFC Cage
articles.description: Paddy Pimblett, Max Holloway and Gable Steveson were each fined $2,500 by the Nevada State Athletic Commission for climbing on the cage during their post-fight celebrations. Michael Bisping called withholding fighter pay a crime. Chael Sonnen sees it differently. Chael explains why the commission wasn't trying to punish the fighters or make an example out of them financially. The $2,500 fines were a warning meant to finally get everyone's attention after fighters had repeatedly been told to stay off the cage. And there is a legitimate reason for the rule. Chael recalls Dan Henderson tearing his ACL during a celebration and another fighter landing on a cameraman and breaking his leg after a backflip. He also explains the complicated liability and insurance questions that arise when someone gets hurt after a fight has officially ended. Then there's Justin Gaethje. Fans may love Gaethje's signature backflip, but Chael admits it makes him nervous every single time. This isn't about taking celebrations out of MMA. It's about safety, liability and enforcing a rule that has been ignored for years. Consider Chael the messenger: stay off the cage. #UFC #PaddyPimblett #MaxHolloway #GableSteveson #ChaelSonnen #MMABad Guy Inc merch now available at https://BadGuyInc.com Click here to subscribe: https://bit.ly/3FrHIPK Follow me on IG: https://bit.ly/3HY7BIE Follow me on Twitter: https://bit.ly/3tvY5J7 Follow me on Threads https://www.threads.com/@sonnench

articles.title: Josh Hokit Knows Something About Tom Aspinall
articles.description: Something strange is happening in the UFC heavyweight division, and Chael Sonnen can't figure out why nobody is talking about it. Tom Aspinall's return is supposed to be imminent. Ciryl Gane holds the interim heavyweight championship. By every conventional understanding of an interim title, Gane should be next in line for Aspinall. So why haven't we heard anything about the rematch? One possibility is simple: Aspinall vs. Gane is already planned for Madison Square Garden and the UFC just hasn't announced it yet. But Josh Hokit is making Chael suspicious. Hokit has openly discussed several options at heavyweight, including Alex Pereira and Sergei Pavlovich, but the fight he wants is Ciryl Gane. Chael wonders why Hokit would pursue the interim champion instead of positioning himself for the winner of Aspinall vs. Gane. Does Hokit know something about Tom Aspinall's return that the rest of us don't? articles.title: Everyone Is Wrong About WWE's Brawl for All
articles.description: WWE's Brawl for All is remembered as one of the worst ideas in professional wrestling history. Chael Sonnen thinks everybody has it wrong. After Bully Ray called the infamous tournament a “stupid idea,” Chael looks back at what Brawl for All actually was, why he couldn't wait to watch it during the Monday Night Wars, and the biggest mistake WWE made with the entire concept. The problem wasn't putting professional wrestlers into legitimate fights. The problem was that WWE never properly communicated to the audience that what they were watching was real. Look at today's landscape. Influencer boxing sells arenas, combat sports dominate social media, and audiences are fascinated by seeing personalities actually fight. Put willing WWE stars into a legitimate tournament today, promote it correctly, and Chael believes Brawl for All could become one of the biggest things in wrestling. The execution had problems. The concept didn't. articles.title: Conor McGregor May Be the Last True Megastar
articles.description: Will the UFC ever produce another superstar as big as Conor McGregor? Chael Sonnen has been debating that question with his producer Ryan but there's another question that may matter even more: does the UFC actually need one? Conor McGregor, Ronda Rousey, Georges St-Pierre and the biggest stars in combat sports made life easy for promoters. They sold tickets, generated mainstream media attention and brought new audiences into the sport. But megastars also consume almost all the attention around them. Chael explains why the departure of one enormous star can create room for four or five others to rise, and why today's UFC may be better positioned with several highly sought-after fighters instead of relying on one athlete to carry the business. From Babe Ruth and Michael Jordan to Hulk Hogan, Steve Austin, The Rock, Muhammad Ali and Mike Tyson, Chael examines how distribution, timing and technology create transcendent sports stars and why the circumstances that created Conor McGregor may never exist again. Maybe there won't be another Conor. articles.title: Why Fighters Should NOT Be Allowed on the Fence #ufc
articles.description: Three fighters reportedly had their pay withheld after violating the UFC's rule against climbing the fence. Daniel Cormier believes fighters work too hard to have their celebration ruined over something like jumping on the cage. Chael Sonnen takes a different position. Chael says there's room to debate whether the rule should exist — but once the rule is in place, it has to be enforced. And he has a very good reason for feeling that way. Justin Gaethje's famous backflip already makes Chael nervous every time he sees it. Chael recalls an event where another fighter attempted a similar celebration, landed on a cameraman, and caused a serious injury. He also remembers Dan Henderson being told to show more excitement after a victory, only for Henderson to jump onto the bottom rope and suffer an ACL injury. That's the bigger issue. If you're competing under the oversight of an athletic commission and you get injured while violating the rules, there can be serious consequences — including responsibility for who pays the medical costs. Chael does question whether withholding an entire fight purse is appropriate. But the underlying rule? He believes it matters. #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #DanielCormier #JustinGaethje #UFCNews #MMAAnalysis #FightGame #CombatSports #UFCRules

articles.title: This Was Ian Garry's One Shot #ufc
articles.description: Ian Garry may have just lost his only opportunity to fight Islam Makhachev for a UFC championship. Dana White has suggested that Garry may never fight for a UFC title again — and that another championship matchup with Islam could be even less likely. Chael Sonnen believes Garry's performance inside the Octagon deserves credit. But there's one thing he can't stop thinking about: why was Ian so concerned with earning Islam's respect? Garry spent valuable moments during and after the fight praising Islam, embracing him, and treating him like a friend rather than the man standing between him and the championship. Chael doesn't have a problem with psychological warfare. In fact, he believes trying to convince an opponent that you're his friend before ultimately attacking is completely fair game. But that's not what Chael believes happened here. The final embrace came after the final bell — and Chael points out that those seconds matter in a championship fight. If Islam remains champion, Garry may have to wait a very long time for another opportunity. And that's why Chael believes this could become the kind of mistake that keeps a fighter awake at night. Garry fought well. But did he waste the most important moments of his career? #IanGarry #IslamMakhachev #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #DanaWhite #UFCNews #MMAAnalysis #UFCChampionship #CombatSports

articles.title: Paddy Pimblett Gained 34 Pounds. So What?
articles.description: For a limited time, our listeners get 50% off FOR LIFE, Free Shipping, AND 3 Free Gifts at Mars Men at https://www.mengotomars.com Paddy Pimblett made the lightweight limit. Then he stepped into the Octagon significantly heavier. Does that make him a “weight bully,” or does it mean he simply played by the rules? Pimblett revealed that he weighed 190 pounds in the cage against Benoît Saint Denis after officially weighing 156 pounds, a 34-pound increase between the weigh-in and fight night. Chael challenges the assumption that gaining that much weight automatically creates an advantage. Carrying additional weight comes with consequences, and making 155 pounds requires enormous discipline, sacrifice and preparation in the first place. The larger question is whether MMA's weigh-in system makes sense at all. If regulators truly want to discourage extreme weight cutting, there are already examples of how to do it. But as long as the rules allow fighters time to rehydrate, athletes are going to search for every competitive advantage available. Paddy followed the rules and made the contracted weight. Chael explains why calling him a bully for doing it misses the point entirely. articles.description: Michael Bisping reacts immediately after UFC Sacramento, where Gregory “RoboCop” Rodrigues stunned Anthony “Fluffy” Hernandez in a brutal five-round main event. Bisping breaks down RoboCop’s takedown defence, punishing calf kicks and relentless pace, Fluffy’s incredible toughness and a potential showdown with Dricus Du Plessis.
